page: Amazon Web Services m6in.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual server built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz, providing 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with two threads per core. The processor features 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 54 MB L3 cache. It incorporates vector and cryptographic instruction sets including AVX, AVX-512 (with VNNI support), AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

The server provides 64.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3.0 GHz, yielding a balanced 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Network throughput is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 25 Gbps. The configuration does not include local NVMe or SSD storage, necessitating network-attached Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) volumes for persistent storage. Hardware graphics acceleration is omitted, with zero GPUs present.

Performance across synthetic and compute-intensive benchmarks aligns consistently within the middle 50% average range. PassMark records an overall CPU score of 21,026.46, with encryption capabilities measuring 14,547.80 and database operations at 7,761.73. Geekbench scores show 1,655.0 for single-core execution and 9,804.0 for multi-core. In memory operations, cached 16 KB read throughput registers at 834.23 GB/sec, while uncached 256 MB reads and writes deliver 97.84 GB/sec and 57.65 GB/sec, respectively. In-memory Redis SET performance demonstrates 15.37 million operations per second, accompanied by a static web serving throughput of 21.96 GB/sec.

On inference workloads, the instance processes small 135M language models effectively at 1,313.36 prompt tokens per second and 244.43 generation tokens per second. Performance diminishes on larger architectures, dropping to 31.78 prompt tokens per second on a medium 7B model, ranking in the lower 25% bracket. Given its 25 Gbps baseline networking and balanced memory footprint, the m6in.4xlarge represents a cost-efficient resource profile for network-bound enterprise services, caching tiers, microservices, backend web servers, and distributed compilation pipelines relying on EBS.
description: Amazon Web Services m6in.4xlarge is a general-purpose, Nitro-based cloud instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8375C x86_64 processor operating at 3.5 GHz. It offers 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores and 64.0 GB of DDR4 memory, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Networking throughput includes a 25 Gbps baseline, while local storage and dedicated GPUs are absent, requiring EBS for persistence. Benchmark results place the server firmly in the middle 50% tier, showing 21,026.46 on PassMark CPU, 9,804.0 on Geekbench multi-core, and 15.37 million operations per second on Redis SET tests. Large-model inference reveals performance limits, yet its strong network baseline and balanced hardware profile make it cost-efficient for web serving, microservices, data caching, and CI/CD compilation.
